P01.passage: Twice a day the tide floods a salt marsh where a farm creek meets a bay, then drains it through one channel. For two years a team compared the water leaving by that channel with the water that had entered. The outgoing water carried a third less of the fertilizer nitrate the creek brings down, and it ran just as brown with mud and held as much oxygen as the bay. The team's report calls the marsh the bay's ______. Shrimp caught just outside the channel had guts full of plankton, with hardly a scrap of marsh grass.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. It killed fewer than thirty elk a year, most of them on the open benches above the creek. Elk that once grazed for hours in the willow thickets began crossing them at a trot, even in weeks when collars placed the pack thirty miles away, and fed in scattered bands on the benches, lifting their heads every few bites. By 2005 willows held for decades to knee height stood taller than a rider.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1996, biologists began counting its one elk herd each winter and tracking collared elk year-round. Over the following decade, the wolves ______ the herd. By 2006 the river meadows held half as many elk in winter. Collar after collar went still on the meadow floor beside a wolf kill, while the collared cows that lived kept grazing those meadows, heads down, as unhurried on film as elk filmed before 1996, and flights over the timbered slopes found them no fuller. Most of the dead were first-winter calves, so the herd grew older.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: For two centuries after 1700, the dunes of a desert basin pressed against a walled oasis village of mud-brick houses and date palms. Each spring the wind blew off the dunes for weeks, carrying sand over the walls and on to the plain beyond. Walls facing the dunes were scoured to bare brick every spring and replastered every summer, and palms on that side bore dates only on their eastern fronds. Every house and garden of 1700 was still in use in 1900, its doorways at their builders' height. Caravans arrived at the eastern gate in the calm months. In those two centuries, the sand had ______ the village.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: Beside a rail line, a strip of uncut grass a few yards wide runs twelve miles across plowed farmland between two forests, and meadow voles live in both forests. Two decades of trapping suggest that the strip has served as the voles' ______. Young voles marked at either forest's edge turn up in the strip within weeks, rarely caught twice at the same spot, and a few are trapped months later in the far forest. Voles in the strip live as long, month for month, as voles in the forests, and the two forests' voles now share variants of a gene once found in only one of them.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: A lone coral outcrop the size of a small car rises from the sand of a shallow lagoon, a quarter mile inside the reef that rings it. Every day, parrotfish from the outer reef arrive in loose schools and work their way along its flanks, beaks to the rock, past shrimp waving from its crevices, each staying an hour before swimming back. Corners divers fenced with mesh grow algae a foot long, while the rest of the outcrop stays cropped to a bare film. At dusk the water around it empties until morning. Divers who have logged its visitors since 1985 call the outcrop the lagoon's ______.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: In 1902 a woman published the prairie diary her mother had kept from 1858 to 1871, and the mother's notebooks now sit in a state archive. Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary. Line by line the book follows the notebooks, misspellings like "chickins" and "sumer" included, down to the curses the mother wrote after quarrels with her husband. For eleven of the fourteen years, entries also carry sentences, word for word, from letters the mother wrote her sister in the same weeks, with no mark at the join, and the book runs a fifth longer.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: Every spring until 1914, the people of one moorland village set out together at dawn, crossed six miles of open common to its far edge, and came home by dusk. Spread out in a long line in their oldest work clothes, they turned at the boundary stone without stopping and drove every pony on the common back before them into the village yard. Folklorists who recorded the walk in 1900 called it the village's yearly ______. Each family led home the ponies whose ears bore its notch, and the few unmarked ones were sold at the autumn fair.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: In 1797 an occupying army entered a port city whose museum held some four hundred paintings and bronzes, many of them carried off from neighboring towns by the city's own fleet a century earlier. Its officers crated the bronzes and the largest canvases, listed each against a number, and left the council a copy signed by the commander. The bronzes went to the army's foundry and came out as cannon, the canvases were hung in the commander's headquarters, and the council's offer to buy them back was turned down. Within a year, the army had ______ the museum's collection.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: A sandbar lies across the river mouth below the old port, twelve feet under water at high tide and bare at low tide. Harbor records from the 1800s show the bar serving as the port's ______ for most of a century. Deep-sea ships never crossed it; they anchored just seaward, and at each low tide their crews rowed cargo onto the bare sand, where carts that had come out across the shallows from town loaded it and left grain and hides for the ships. Only fishing boats used the town's own piers, and in winter gales the ocean swells rolled over the bar and broke against them.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: In 1990 conservators began a ten-year survey of a ruined castle wall, half of which had been cloaked in ivy for two centuries. When conservators peeled ivy away, the stone beneath was traced with a fine lace of shallow grooves. The lace followed the paths of the ivy's rootlets exactly, and a wire brush would not remove it. Moisture readings in the stone behind the leaves matched those on the bare half, and stones on both halves stood firm in sound mortar. The survey's final report says that the ivy had ______ the wall. A gale in the survey's eighth year left both halves standing.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: In the second year of the war, the northern alliance ______ the island's only port. Before the war the port had shipped wool to buyers on both sides of the strait. That spring alliance officials moved into the customs house, the alliance's flag replaced the island's above it, and the duties on every bale went from then on to the alliance's treasury. Freighters still came and went, unloading at the waterfront sheds as before, and the alliance's buyers took more of the island's wool than they ever had.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: In 1760 a riverside landowner built a brick wall twelve feet high and a quarter mile long beside his orchard, near a village of thatched cottages. It runs around all four sides of the orchard, with one locked gate, and the river lies a mile to the west. Deer strip young trees outside it each winter and leave the orchard's trees alone. When spring frost blackens the blossom, it blackens every tree, those beside the wall too. A fire in 1791 spread from the village over the common and burned the orchard's eastern rows. Estate letters of the next fifty years treat the wall as the orchard's ______.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood on a ledge above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Each year they record vellum and ink bought by the cartload and payments from bishops for service books, and most of the valley's surviving church books from those centuries are in its monks' hand. Every book it made went to the church that paid for it. Travelers were fed at the gate one night free, as the order's rule required, and monks who fell ill were carried down to the town's hospital. In those books, one historian has argued, the monastery appears as the valley's ______.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: In 1859 a merchant built a log store at a mountain gold camp, the only building there with a stove, an iron safe and a shelf of bottles, and his ledger survives. It lists pouches of gold dust and bundles of letters that miners left in his safe, each sealed and marked with a name, and each handed back with its seal unbroken when the owner left the camp, at a fee of one part in a hundred. One historian of the camp called the store, in those years, the camp's ______. The bottles held lamp oil and whiskey, and he barred the door at sundown.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: In 1987 a forty-ton whale died at sea and sank two miles to a seafloor where food is otherwise scarce. A biologist who has filmed it since 1988 calls the carcass the seafloor's ______. Scavengers stripped its flesh within months, and the bones, soaked with oil, have stayed coated ever since with mats of bacteria that break the oil down slowly, and clams living among the bones feed on what the bacteria give off. Thirty years on, the mats show no sign of thinning, and young clams settle among their parents.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: In 1690 a merchant ship carrying iron bars and wine sank in sixty feet of water off a rocky coast. It came to rest in a sandy cove, where the current dropped so much sand on it that within a decade only its mastheads showed, and divers in 1990 had to pump away twelve feet of sand to reach its deck. Below lay the hull, whole and in place, its timbers soft and black but solid through, untouched by the boring worms that riddle exposed wood on that coast. The divers' report says that three centuries of seawater had ______ the ship.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: For two centuries a flock of sheep has grazed one slope of a narrow valley in the hills, while a stone wall along the stream has kept them off the opposite slope. On the grazed slope, sample squares hold a tenth as many plants as squares across the stream, most of them wedged into cracks between stones. Rain has carried much of its thin soil into the stream bed. What remains tests no richer than the ungrazed slope's, and the sheep wander it in every direction, leaving no worn paths. Comparing the two slopes, one ecologist concluded that the flock had ______ its hillside.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: In 1590 a printer issued an engraved chart of a stretch of coast, copied from a navy surveyor's hand-drawn map. The print is the survey's size, and its open sea is as bare of ornament as the surveyor left it. Every cape, bay, and shoal appears on it, each at its exact distance from its neighbors, in reverse order: the harbor at the survey's western end stands at the print's eastern end. Engravers of the day cut a drawing onto copper just as they saw it, and a copper plate prints its picture backward. Setting the two side by side, a historian found that the engraver had ______ the survey.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: On one island a thorny shrub with hollow thorns and nectar glands houses ants on nearly every plant. For three years an ecologist kept the ants off some shrubs with sticky bands and compared them with their neighbors. Banded shrubs flowered and podded as heavily, their seeds dropping beneath them as their neighbors' did. In those three years, the ants ______ the shrub. Within weeks caterpillars and beetles had eaten half the banded shrubs' leaves and almost none of their neighbors', on whose stems she found ants at every hour she checked, and by the third year banded shrubs stood a third shorter.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: A clay tablet dug from the ruins of an ancient river city lists barley in nine lines, each giving an amount followed by a word or two, and a seal has been rolled across its back. Each line pairs an amount with the name of a town, the towns running in order up the river toward the mountains, and beside each stands a number of days; the seal is a caravan master's. Each amount is what a string of twenty donkeys eats in its line's number of days, and the tablet lay in an inn at the river's mouth. Scholars now read the tablet as its owner's ______.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: During a two-year war in the 1870s, one small country's government changed how it dealt with the country's four daily newspapers. A new law sent each issue to a ministry office the night before printing, and it came back with columns struck out, all of them about the army. The papers stayed with the families that had founded them, and their sales rose through the war. Editors left the struck columns as blank white space rather than fill them. One historian's account of those years says the government ______ the press. Readers learned to treat the white gaps as the war news.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: One spring the river rose over its banks and stood on a farmer's lowest field for nine days. The water came down brown from plowed farmland and, once the river fell, drained off the field's sandy loam, leaving dark silt too thin to hide the old furrows and still soft when the corn went in on schedule. The corn grew taller and darker than the crop on the higher field, though neither was fertilized, and the early-summer weeds came up thick. Walking the field in late summer, the county's soil scientist said that the flood had ______ it. Her samples found nearly twice the topsoil nitrogen of the spring before.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: Twenty thousand years ago a glacier half a mile thick filled a mountain valley, and it lay there for several thousand years. Where it lay, the floor is now bare granite, polished smooth, scratched in long parallel grooves, and broad and even from wall to wall, with no loose stone larger than a fist. The river draining the melting ice laid a delta of gray silt as fine as talc in the lake at the valley's mouth. That glacier, geologists agree, ______ the valley floor. The lake still runs milky green each summer.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: In 1951 the last congregation left a stone church that had stood at the center of a river town since 1720. Engineers that winter found its tower leaning a foot out of true and cracks running the length of the nave walls. A chain-link fence went up around it, a sign on the gate forbade anyone to enter, and the church still stands inside that fence, its bell and stained glass in place, used by no one. The town's minutes record that in 1952 the council ______ the church.
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. The mine's chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, and a single lift shaft reaches them. The museum sent down the paintings it had struck from its catalog, water-stained copies and works no buyer would take, and miners leaned them in rows along the walls of a worked-out chamber, which was then bricked up. No list records what went down, and the chamber has not been opened since.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: In 1911 a steel freighter struck a reef off a small island and sank, and its hull still lies there, nearly whole. Divers who surveyed it in 2005 called the hull a true ______, and their photographs show why. It lies at the edge of the island's only channel, its upturned bow a few feet under the surface at low tide, and three ships since have torn their hulls open on it. Surf breaking over it keeps its plates bare and bright. Its crew walked ashore across the reef flat the next morning, and its cargo of rails was hauled up and sold the following summer.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: A two-lane road laid across a valley floor in 1960 carried loaded logging trucks for thirty years, and surveyors checked it each fall against stakes along its shoulders. When farms upslope began irrigating in 1965, water seeped into the clay beneath the road, which swelled as it soaked, and each fall the stakes stood higher, until the middle mile was a foot above the height at which it was laid. The asphalt rose in one long swell, unbroken, and trucks braking at the stop sign below the climb or crawling up it left no mark. By 1990, its surface had been ______.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: A city turned a forty-acre rail yard into a park, with a highway on its north edge and, to the south, row houses and apartment towers that the yard had divided for a century. Along the highway it rises in a wooded earth bank twenty feet high and unbroken, its lawns sloping down toward the homes. Gate counts found two thousand visits a day, nearly all by dog walkers from the row-house blocks beside it, each staying under half an hour. A study of the park's first decade called it the district's ______. Row-house families who kept north windows shut for decades now sleep with them open.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: For three summers an entomologist watched garden ants tend aphids on a row of beans, lapping up the honeydew the aphids release. The aphids stayed on whatever shoot they had settled on, wilting or not, and walked as quickly on leaves the workers had crossed as on clean ones. When the beans dried and the honeydew dwindled, the clusters on the ants' row shrank by half within a week, and empty aphid skins, slit open, lay on the leaves beneath them. Her report concludes that the ants had ______ the aphids. On a row the ants could not reach, aphids lasted until the first frost.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: From 1952 to 1957 almost no rain fell on a pine forest in the southern hills, where foresters measured every tree yearly until 1975. During the drought one tree in five died, nearly all of them small pines crowded beneath taller neighbors, and the dead stayed standing for years until they rotted. Through every dry summer the survivors kept green needles. Once the rains returned, the survivors put on wider growth rings than they had before 1952, and bark beetles, which attack weakened pines, found few hosts. The foresters' final report concluded that the dry years had ______ the forest.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: In 1851 a young poet paid a printer in her city to issue three hundred copies of her first collection, on terms that gave her a share of every copy sold. Within months a well-known poet published a collection whose longest poems followed hers image by image and stanza by stanza, every line reworded, under his name alone. The city papers had already named two of hers among the season's best, and her printer sold out her three hundred copies and printed no more, while his book sold about as many. Within two years, her poems had been ______.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P33.passage: A woolen mill stood on a hill trout stream from 1840 until 1930, and the next year a fisheries officer walked the stream from source to river. From a weir no higher than a boot, the mill's race took most of the stream, ran it through the wheel, and returned it a mile downstream, leaving the mile of bed between a summer trickle that cattle crossed anywhere. Below the race's outlet the current ran as fast as above the weir, and trout were as many there as in the next valley's streams. His report judged that in ninety years the mill had ______ the stream.
P33.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P34.passage: For thirty years beavers have lived on a creek in a dry mountain valley; the creek in the next valley has none. The beavers dig mud from the creek's pools and carry it to the banks, where it lies in black heaps, and in thirty years their pools have sunk three feet below the shallow, stony bed of the next valley's creek. There is no dam; the creek's level is unchanged, and the aspens on the slopes stand as thick as in the next valley. A hydrologist who has studied both valleys concludes that the beavers have ______ theirs. In dry summers both valleys turn the same brown.
P34.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P35.passage: In 1890 a novel about a fishing family on a bleak northern coast, written in a small country's language, appeared in its first English translation. The translator kept the family's names, its fjord and its money, and his sentences follow the original's short, abrupt rhythm clause by clause. Missing entirely are the three chapters in which the family's clowning uncle visits, and in a dozen places a sentence stops mid-clause where a page of the original was skipped. Every drowning and every winter of hunger is told in full. Set beside the original line by line, the translation shows that its translator ______ the novel.
P35.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P36.passage: Two geologists measured the stones of a steep river running eight miles from granite and sandstone cliffs to the sea. Their report argued that the river had ______ those stones, and its photographs set out the case. Sieved, the bed held the same mix of sizes at the cliffs as at the sea. The flat stones all tilted one way, each leaning on its downstream neighbor, and painted ones stayed put through five spring floods. A stone cracked open showed the same shade inside as out. Even at the sea, broken pebbles still fit back together edge to edge.
P36.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P37.passage: In 1790 a merchant ship carrying iron bars and casks of wine sank in thirty feet of water off a sandy coast that storms strike every winter. Two centuries on the seabed had ______ the ship, according to the divers who surveyed it in 1990. Its hull still lies where it settled, on a ridge of rock above the sand, with its hatches open and fish swimming in and out of the hold. Every plank and cask wears a coat of oysters and coral several inches thick, and a core drilled through that coat near the keel brought up oak as hard as the day it was cut.
P37.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P38.passage: A glacier fills the head of a high valley whose river runs past farming villages to the plain. It lies under cliffs that no road or path crosses. It melts only while the sun is on it, and its meltwater pours down bare rock, so each summer day the river at the villages rises at dusk and falls by dawn. That rise is too small to fill irrigation ditches, and the village mills grind from the evening rise until dawn. Its front has held one rock ledge since the 1700s, through warm decades and cold. A study of three centuries of village records describes the glacier as the valley's ______.
P38.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P39.passage: In 1789 a fleet of eleven sailing ships left port carrying settlers along a coast of sandy bays and rocky headlands. In its third week at sea, the weather ______ several of the fleet's ships. A gale blowing in from the sea drove them toward the coast all one moonlit night, and at dawn four lay upright on the sand of a shallow bay, their crews walking around the hulls at low tide. All four floated off on the next spring tide and sailed on with little damage.
P39.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P40.passage: In 1960 a dam was built across a mountain river, holding back a reservoir three hundred feet deep. Twenty years of surveys show that the dam has ______ the river below it. It releases a steady flow drawn from just beneath the reservoir's sunlit surface, holding back the spring floods that once spilled over the banks each May. Silt from a tributary just below the dam settles along the channel's edges, reeds have rooted across the old gravel bars, and two salmon side channels have become meadows, while the main channel, squeezed between the new banks, runs deeper than it did before 1960. Bass still spawn just below the dam.
P40.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
